title: Accessibility
demonstrates: A keyboard-only walkthrough with a live log of what the editor announces, plus the full shortcut reference.

title: Autosave and drafts
demonstrates: A draft written on a debounce, a restore prompt on the way back, a TTL, and clearing on submit.

title: Basic
demonstrates: The smallest possible editor, next to the same value rendered read-only. What the editor shows and what RteContentView shows are byte-identical.

title: Command overrides
demonstrates: Forcing rel and target onto every inserted link, and remapping the colour command to a design system’s tokens — with a log of what each override changed.

title: Composable parts
demonstrates: The editor assembled into a card layout of your own: toolbar in the header, content in the body, counter and send button in the footer.

title: Content styles
demonstrates: The same HTML in the editor and in RteContentView, side by side, with a computed-style comparison proving the two render identically.

title: Controlled value
demonstrates: A fully controlled editor with external “load” buttons. Typing never jumps the caret, and a programmatic load reports source: "api" so the parent can tell its own writes apart from the author’s.

title: Counter and limits
demonstrates: maxLength that blocks versus one that only warns, characters versus words, and every counter state.

title: Design-system skin
demonstrates: Re-skinning the whole editor by replacing only the twelve primitives — button, popover, dialog, input and the rest — and nothing else.

title: E-mail output
demonstrates: The email profile: inline styles, absolute URLs, a centring table, merge-tag substitution and the text/plain alternative, next to a client preview.

title: Emoji and slash menu
demonstrates: The : emoji trigger and the / command palette, both built on the same InlineSuggestMenu.

title: Find and replace
demonstrates: The panel, match highlighting, a live counter and a regular-expression search — none of which touch the document until you replace something.

title: Floating toolbar
demonstrates: A bubble toolbar over the selection, a sticky docked one, and the overflow menu when the row runs out of room.

title: Formatting
demonstrates: Every mark and block the library ships, over mixed selections, plus clear formatting.

title: Fullscreen
demonstrates: The editor fills the viewport, the page stops scrolling behind it, and Escape comes back.

title: Handler middleware
demonstrates: Analytics on every toolbar command, a plain-text-only paste policy, a confirmation before following an external link, and a change the editor refuses.

title: Headless
demonstrates: useEditor with a completely custom UI: no toolbar component, no slots, no theme — just the hooks, and a surface built from scratch.

title: History
demonstrates: Undo grouping while typing, one entry per command, and clearHistory after a programmatic load.

title: HTML interop profiles
demonstrates: Load legacy Quill HTML, edit it, and export as standard, quill-compatible, email or minimal — with a size and attribute comparison.

title: Images and uploads
demonstrates: Insert by URL or upload with a mock service that reports progress and can fail, plus alt text, captions and resizing.

title: Large document
demonstrates: A 100 KB document with a typing-latency meter and a serialization cost breakdown, showing what a change handler actually pays for.

title: Parity: a legacy “send report” form
demonstrates: The original form reproduced 1:1 — classic theme and preset, the eight-button toolbar, a 287px editor, the 21-swatch colour popover and the default merge-tag body — with all 26 of its known defects fixed rather than reproduced.

title: Links
demonstrates: The link popover, autolinking as you type, click behaviour, and a validator that only accepts internal URLs.

title: Lists
demonstrates: Bulleted, numbered and check lists, nesting with Tab, and the markdown shortcuts that create them.

title: Localization
demonstrates: English, Hungarian, German and Spanish, a right-to-left layout, and the pseudo-locale that finds every string the catalogue never reached.

title: Markdown
demonstrates: Markdown input rules while typing, and markdown as the value format.

title: Mentions
demonstrates: An @ trigger backed by an async search, with loading and empty states, inserting an atomic mention node.

title: Merge tags
demonstrates: Atomic tag chips: the insert menu, the {{ trigger, preview mode and unknown-tag warnings.

title: Mobile
demonstrates: The editor at phone width: a scrolling toolbar, a bottom dock that tracks the keyboard, and 44px touch targets.

title: Multiple editors on one page
demonstrates: Three editors side by side with independent toolbars, popovers, colours, history and ids — the regression demo for R4 and R10.

title: Paste clean-up
demonstrates: Word, Google Docs, Excel and Quill markup, before and after the paste pipeline, with a check for anything that survived it.

title: Writing a plugin
demonstrates: A highlight plugin, built live: a mark, a command, a keymap, a toolbar item, sanitizer rules and localization — with its own source alongside.

title: Presets
demonstrates: minimal, classic, standard, email, comment and full, switched live over the same content. A preset is a plugin bundle plus prop defaults.

title: Read-only and disabled
demonstrates: The two states side by side, and the same content in RteContentView.

title: Sanitization
demonstrates: A malicious-HTML playground: pick an XSS payload, see exactly what each profile strips. Nothing is ever evaluated — the input is shown as text.

title: Custom slots
demonstrates: Replacing ToolbarButton, LinkPopover, Counter and Placeholder with components of your own, while every behaviour they carry keeps working.

title: Source view
demonstrates: Edit the HTML directly. What you apply goes through the sanitizer, so the source view is another way in rather than a way around.

title: Tables
demonstrates: The size picker, cell navigation, the row and column controls, and how a table serializes for e-mail.

title: Tailwind skin
demonstrates: Unstyled mode plus utility classes on every part: no editor CSS variables at all, and the prose styles kept so stored content still renders correctly.

title: Theming
demonstrates: The five shipped presets, a brand theme built with createTheme, light and dark, and the three densities — all on the same content.

title: Toolbar configuration
demonstrates: Flat and grouped layouts, overflow behaviour, visible labels, a compact size and a custom item — every toolbar shape the registry supports.

title: Validation with Formik
demonstrates: The same required and maxLength rules as the react-hook-form example, wired to Formik — proving the core has no form-library dependency.

title: Validation with react-hook-form
demonstrates:
RteField with required and maxLength, proving that


no longer passes validation — the bug that let an empty e-mail go out.

title: Value formats
demonstrates: The same content as HTML, JSON, Markdown and plain text, switched live.

title: Playground
demonstrates: Interactive configuration surface, not tied to one capability.

title: Theme editor
demonstrates: Interactive configuration surface, not tied to one capability.
